key_insight: Stabilizing slight tetragonal distortion in smaller BaTiO3 nanoparticles boosts covalency, polarization, and charge retention, enabling stronger lead-free piezoelectric nanogenerator performance.
engineering_relevance: This suggests nanoparticle size and bonding control can be used to tune hybrid piezoelectric-triboelectric devices for higher output in self-powered electronics.
method: Ligand-assisted sol-gel synthesis of BaTiO3 nanoparticles
Structural validation by XRD, Raman, and pair distribution function analysis
DFT calculations to assess Ti–O covalency, orbital hybridization, and polarization behavior
evidence_signal: BTO-900 (~54 nm) showed ~100 V open-circuit voltage and ~29 μJ stored energy, while BTO-1200 (~104 nm) achieved up to ~649 μW cm-2 power density and ~181 μA short-circuit current.
watch_item: The best voltage/energy and best current/power came from different particle sizes, so device optimization will likely require balancing polarization strength, charge trapping, and impedance matching.
paper_title: Small Distortions, Big Polarization: Tetragonal BaTiO3 Nanoparticles for High-Performance Piezoelectric Nanogenerators
